title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It has a twin, which differs only in what A does on a 1. This page lists what is established, sorted by what each result rests on; the counter at its left end is understood, the work zone that drives it is not.
verdict: The question is open. It halts only when F reads a 1, which has not happened in 2·1010 steps. The left end is a binary counter whose increment is proved in Lean; the work zone that drives it is not understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Three shift rules for all n and any surrounding tape: E crosses (110)^n leaving (010)^n, D crosses (011)^n leaving (001)^n, and B crosses (100)^n leaving (101)^n.

claims.title: The increment of the left counter
claims.text: For every n and any tape around it, L 1000 (1010)^n C>1 1 R reaches L 1010 1 (0001)^n 0 D> R in 12n+8 steps: C walks left over n one-digits 1010, turns the zero-digit 1000 into a one, and B walks back turning each one-digit into a zero-digit. A1 is not used, so the same theorem holds for both twins.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 182 cells have been visited and 71 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
Where the twins differ
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps A reads a 1 only 11 times, always with 0s on both sides; F reads only 0s, followed by a 0.

claims.title: A binary counter at the left end
claims.text: Whenever the head is at least 8 cells right of the counter, the tape from the left end reads 1010101101010110, then 4-cell digits 1010 (one) and 1000 (zero), then 11. Read as a binary number (least significant digit on the right) this counter goes up at almost every change. From step 6.3·106 to 109 the decoded value changes 529,577 times; 529,571 changes are increases, 4 are overflows where the counter gains a digit (18 → 21 digits), and 2 are not classified. At 109 steps it has 20 digits.

claims.title: Not decided by n-gram CPS up to width 14
claims.text: The n-gram Closed Position Set decider (tools/c/ngramcps.c) with equal widths 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14, plain and with the fixed-length (1) and LRU history augmentations, either reaches a halting local configuration (UNKNOWN) or stops at 3·107 local configurations: it does not prove non-halting at these settings.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: Late in the run the tape is made of long stretches of (0 1)^n, (0^3 1)^n and (1^2 0)^n; both ends grow, the right one by single cells at irregular times (e.g. 2a: cell 175 at step 4.7·108). The stretches (0 1)^n and (0^3 1)^n are the digits 1010 and 1000 of the left binary counter read with another phase (see below).

claims.title: A work zone between the counter and a growing (110)^n block
claims.text: Right of the counter the head works in a zone of 20 to 40 cells of words 10, 1000, 110, turning thousands of times between two increments of the counter; at the right end a block (110)^n grows by one word at each right record (for 2a, n = 12, 13, 14 at the right records at 4.7·108, 5.8·108 and 9.6·108 steps). What the work zone computes between two increments is not known.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No macro description of the run is known yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two machines that part at step 132
html: This machine and its twin, 1RB1RD_1LC0RD_... (2a) and 1RB1RF_1LC0RD_... (2b), differ only in what state A does when it reads a 1: 2a goes to D, 2b to F. A reads a 1 very rarely (11 times in the first 109 steps of 2a, 17 times for 2b), the first time at step 132. After that the two runs differ, but they are built the same way.

sections.heading: A binary counter fed by a busy work zone
html: The left end of the tape is a binary counter. After a short fixed prefix (1010101101010110) it is a row of 4-cell digits: 1010 means 1 and 1000 means 0, least significant on the right, ended by 11. To add one, the head arrives in state C on that 11, runs left over the trailing ones, changes the first zero into a one, and runs back in state B changing the ones it passed into zeros. Lean proves this move for any number of trailing ones; in simulation the counter goes up at almost every change (529,571 increases in 109 steps).

Right of the counter is a work zone of a few dozen cells where the head zigzags thousands of times between two increments, and at the right end a block of 110 words that grows by one word now and then. The stretches (0 1)^n and (0^3 1)^n seen on the tape are just the counter's ones and zeros, read with a different phase.

sections.heading: What the work zone does is unknown
html: The counter is understood; the work zone is not. It decides how many steps pass between increments and when the 110 block grows, and it is where F would have to read a 1 for the machine to stop. A proof either way needs the macro rule of the work zone: which configurations it returns to when it hands a carry to the counter, as a function of the counter's digits. That has not been found.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).
After 109 steps the tape spans 182 cells (42 left of the start, 133 right), with a density of 1s of 0.39.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Binary counter fed by a work zone (1RB1R?_1LC0RD_1RE0LD_0RE0LF_0LB0RA_0LC--- twins)
summary: Twin 2a: a proved binary counter of 4-cell digits at the left end, incremented by a busy work zone whose rule is unknown, and a growing (110)^n block on the right; open.
